properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at Gullwick Docks
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; never looks anyone in the eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line; terse, goes back to her net when done talking
properties.wants: Never to row at night; will row the party by day for two silver
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm. Hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water.

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

changes.why: New named NPC voiced by the GM.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net.

changes.why: Where the party met her.

sources.quote: She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: She works the boat at pier four.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago, the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela links the mine's flooding to the bell.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: Fact is about the mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Entrance is a black mouth in the chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side; warm air smelling of church and old candle wax. About thirty paces in the tunnel floods with warm black water, with wet hymn-book pages floating and stuck to the walls.
properties.state: closed, tunnel flooded with warm water

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: GM's description of the mine.

change.name: Hymn-book pages marked M. Brand in Saltmere

properties.statement: Wet hymn-book pages float in the flooded Saltmere tunnel; one, with a hymn about the sea giving back what it takes, has "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Physical clue found at the mine.

sources.quote: Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Clue is located at the mine.

properties.what_changed: Teo believes the pencilled "M. Brand" on a hymn page at Saltmere is Mira's handwriting, so she was there.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Teo's claim ties his goal to the mine; the GM only narrated the name.

change.name: Is Maren part of the cult?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect harbor-master Maren Vosk is behind the choir. Only a player theory so far.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Players' theory, tracked as a thread only.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one.

changes.why: The theory is about Maren.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay: just the bell tower and two broken arches, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water, like a congregation, and vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: GM's descriptions of the chapel.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: The bell rang again, louder, and the GM advanced the clock to 3 of 6.

properties.statement: Fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Local legend; the GM did not confirm it, so it stays a rumor, not an NPC.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks; fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New location where the party rests.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks; generous and teasing with the party
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years; says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: New named NPC voiced by the GM.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: He runs the inn.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Where the table last saw him.

change.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Harbor-master Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram's account of Maren's past.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her.

changes.why: Fact is about Maren.

properties.next_step: Row out with Sela at first light and dive to the drowned chapel at low tide, by day only.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: The party's agreed plan for the bell thread.

properties.what_changed: Teo believes the pencilled "M. Brand" on a hymn page at Saltmere is Mira's handwriting, so she was there. He plans to go to the drowned chapel, where he thinks the hymns came from.

sources.quote: Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.

changes.why: Teo's plan to follow Mira's trail to the chapel.
